children: Gold edges up in early Asia trade as markets weigh a pullback in oil prices. If crude's declines hold, that could ease the inflation fears that have sent bond yields up and stoked rate-hike expectations, weighing on the precious metal. Analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, say rate cuts hold the key to interest in gold, as lower bond yields would divert investment into the nonyielding, safe-haven asset. For now, they see further decline as likely in 4Q as dollar strength meets a hawkish turn in Fed policy. That said, geopolitical risks remain high and central bank purchases continue, both of which will ensure a strong floor under around the $3,800/ounce level. Gold ticks up 0.2% to $4,362/ounce. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
